the development of novel leaky-wave antennas based on substrate integrated waveguide technology.

the development of a new type of leaky-wave antenna, with flexible control of the complex propagation factor, which is compatible with planar printed circuit technology and is suitable for low-cost, low profile, high gain applications.
the development of new planar leaky-wave structures that provide flexible control of the real and imaginary propagation constants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presented leaky-wave antenna is a low-cost, low profile, simply fed, easy to manufacture, and highly integrable solution for high-gain, frequency-scanning applications, and is a promising candidate for future wireless communication systems.

the proposed antenna topology is a low profile, low cost and easy to integrate leaky-wave antenna with a flexible control of the complex propagation parameter, which is a key parameter for beam-scanning applications, and that it can be easily integrated in planar printed circuit boards.

the presented antenna concept provides a new degree of freedom to independently and continuously control the antenna beam pointing angle and the main lobe beam width, which is of great importance in modern antenna applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel planar leaky-wave antenna with the capability to independently and flexibly control the real and the imaginary part of the complex propagation factor.

this paper demonstrates a leaky-wave structure that can be used as a building block in a phased array system, where the radiation angle can be controlled by varying the propagation constant, which in turn can be independently controlled through two parameters: the number of metallic vias and the spacing between them.

the proposed antenna can provide a flexible control of the complex propagation coefficient of the leaky-mode, which allows the independent control of the antenna pointing angle, main-lobe beamwidth, and radiation efficiency.
